meanings.note: Moi aussi = me too. Invariable French adverb meaning 'also'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Tu déjeunes aussi avec Dany Boon.
examples.trans: You're also having lunch with Dany Boon.

examples.text: Tu déjeunes aussi avec Dany Boon demain.
examples.trans: You're also having lunch with Dany Boon tomorrow.

meanings.note: Core French preposition meaning 'with', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.
examples.trans: And tomorrow you're having lunch with Audiard.

meanings.note: avoir peur = to be afraid, avoir raison = to be right, avoir 40 ans = to be 40

meanings.en: helper verb of the passé composé
meanings.note: J'ai appelé = I called. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.

meanings.en: il y a = there is, there are
meanings.note: Fixed expression. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.
Sorrow or grief caused by loss.
A cause of sadness or distress.

examples.text: Oui, il faut se battre contre le chagrin.
examples.trans: Yes, we must fight against sorrow.

meanings.note: Entirely or completely, strengthening a description.

examples.text: Tu as complètement perdu la tête!
Gabriel, tu as complètement perdu la tête!
examples.trans: Gabriel, you've completely lost your mind!

meanings.note: D' before a vowel. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
le film de Tarantino = Tarantino's film
Also 'some': du sucre. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
À demain = see you tomorrow. Invariable French adverb meaning 'tomorrow'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.
examples.trans: And tomorrow you're having lunch with Audiard.

meanings.note: dire la vérité à quelqu'un = to tell someone the truth
dire à quelqu'un; dis-lui = tell her/him

examples.text: Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir.

meanings.note: en retard = late, en vacances = on holiday

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

examples.trans: It's just a job to make my family happy.

meanings.note: Fire, flame or a source of heat.

Les chagrins, les hommes, tout part en fumée.

meanings.note: An adult man. The h is not pronounced: l’homme.
Human being in some general uses.

examples.text: Le rôle est pour un homme.
examples.trans: The part is for a man.

examples.text: Ils ont pensé que ce serait mieux avec un homme.
examples.trans: They thought it would be better with a man.

meanings.note: for masculine nouns, and in impersonal phrases: il y a
Also in fixed phrases: il y a. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'he'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
Not acting with proper care or responsibility; same singular spelling for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Ils vont encore dire qu'on est irresponsables.
examples.trans: They're going to say we're irresponsible again.

examples.trans: I have never seen such a demanding actor!

examples.text: Il ne répond jamais au téléphone pendant le week-end.
examples.trans: He never answers the phone during the weekend.

meanings.note: J' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'I'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

meanings.note: Play a role or act in a production.
Play, as children do.

meanings.note: merci beaucoup = thank you very much

examples.text: Merci beaucoup pour votre aide précieuse aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: Thank you very much for your valuable help today.

examples.text: Je te dis mille fois merci pour ce beau rôle!
examples.trans: I thank you a thousand times for this great role!

meanings.note: Stressed form: pour moi, avec moi. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'me'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.trans: It's like a dream for me.

meanings.note: ma before a feminine noun, mon before a vowel

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

Qui parle?. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'who'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.trans: I'm the one who trained you!

examples.trans: You're not leaving. I'm the one firing you!

examples.trans: What are the two of you talking about?

+ infinitive: savoir monter. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to know; to know how to'.

examples.trans: Do you know where he is?
